name: NASC
description: Tutoring, homework support, and one-to-one academic assistance for coursework across subjects. Often the first stop for "I don't understand the material" or "I'm falling behind" situations.

name: NLC
description: Study space, computers, software, and printing. Good option when a student needs the tools or environment to get work done, not necessarily academic instruction.
whatToBring: Assignment or files to print/work on

name: ITS
description: Help with computer access, technology problems, and IT accounts when a broken or unreliable device is affecting a student's coursework.

name: DAS
description: Handles accommodations, interpreting, captioning, and access concerns. Any time an accommodation isn't working, or a student doesn't know how to request one, this is the office that should know.

name: myAccess
description: The online portal students use to manage and request accommodations.

name: Starfish
description: Tool many students use to book appointments and connect with academic support services.

name: Faculty / Office Hours
description: The instructor is often the fastest and most direct source of help on course content, assignment expectations, and grading questions.
whatToBring: Specific questions about the assignment or material

name: Academic Advisor
description: Helps students think through course load, dropping/withdrawing, probation, degree requirements, and bigger-picture academic decisions. This is the right resource whenever a student is considering a decision with lasting consequences.
whatToBring: Specific concern or decision to discuss

name: Financial Aid
description: Supports students whose finances are affecting their ability to stay in school — textbooks, tuition, emergency funding, and related questions.

name: Residence Life
description: Handles roommate conflict, housing discomfort, and living-situation concerns.

name: Career Services
description: Helps students explore majors and career paths when they're unsure what they want to do.

name: Student Life
description: Clubs, organizations, and events — the go-to resource for students who feel disconnected or want to get more involved on campus.

name: Counseling & Psychological Services
description: Professional mental health support for students in distress, including severe mental health crises. Peer mentors should connect students here rather than counseling them directly.

name: Title IX / Care Team
fullName: Title IX Office / Student Care Team
description: Trained staff for reports of sexual misconduct, harassment, discrimination, and stalking. Peer mentors should connect students here rather than investigating themselves.

name: Campus Public Safety
description: Campus-based safety response for threats, immediate danger, or situations requiring an in-person safety presence.

name: Dean of Students
description: The staff escalation point named in your program's protocol. Peer mentors should follow their program's specific reporting chain for Red-level situations — confirm who this is during training.

name: Emergency Services
description: Call for any medical emergency or immediate danger to life.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: National 24/7 hotline for suicide risk and mental health crises. Call or text 988. Deaf and hard-of-hearing callers can use videophone or the chat option at 988lifeline.org.
